crime: Every evening from eight to nine, a girl sat in the library knitting one grey square for a blanket. Seeing {WITCH_NAME} watching, she held out the needles to her, then asked her to join the squares. At nine each night {WITCH_NAME} held out her hand from the lounge sofa, and by her Magic the finished square sailed down from the library into her palm. She joined it into the blanket on her knees while the girls watched.

When it was done, the knitter lifted the blanket off {WITCH_NAME}'s knees in the dining hall and wrapped it round a girl shivering at the end of the table. "It's only squares. I can knit more." The girls clapped.
When {WITCH_NAME} was nine, she had spent all winter knitting a scarf for her mother. Her mother laid it in a drawer without unfolding it, and {WITCH_NAME} had not knitted since.
While the girls clapped, she kept her empty hands in her lap. After supper, alone on the bunk in her cell, she knitted a grey square.

A little after eight, in the library, she wrapped the grey yarn twice round the knitter's throat and pulled until the girl was still. She slid the few rows off the needles and wound them back onto the ball. By half past eight she was on the sofa among the girls. At nine she held out her hand as always, and a finished square sailed into her palm.

At half past nine the prisoners found the knitter on the library window seat, yarn at her throat, needles bare. She had finished her square at nine, they decided, and been strangled after, while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them.

In the trial court, a prisoner laid that last square against the blanket round the shivering girl's shoulders. It was a finger narrower than any of the knitter's. It was not hers, the prisoner realized. It had flown in from wherever it lay; the knitter was dead before nine.
fields.epitaph: After the drawer she knitted only one thing, and made sure it would pass for someone else's.
fields.epithet: The Scarf Folded Away in a Drawer
execution: Two iron knitting needles as tall as the gallery rise, a grey scarf hanging from them. She sits chained beneath it, wrists fixed, palms turned up.
The needles knit the last row, then drive down through the scarf into her chest. The finished scarf slides off the needles and settles round her shoulders.
She slumps beneath it and goes still. Her palms stay turned up, empty.

magic.name: Come to Hand
magic.text: Whatever she wants flies on its own into her outstretched hand.
